title: Architecting a Quad-Level Practical Education Framework for Autonomous Molecular Feature Extraction and AI-Driven Therapeutics Design
content: Higher education programs focusing on medical informatics and intelligent biomedical engineering are actively incorporating artificial intelligence methodologies for pharmaceutical development. However, laboratory coursework frequently continues to frame molecular machine learning as basic supervised curve-fitting on diminutive, arbitrarily partitioned datasets. This manuscript presents a novel instructional laboratory architecture that adapts an active research initiative—specifically, the autonomous pre-training of visual molecular features via graph structure bootstrapping (MolRL)—into a comprehensive four-stage undergraduate curriculum integrated with applied engineering principles. The pedagogical architecture is underpinned by four core concepts: constructive alignment, progressive experiential learning, the integration of teaching with research, and the CDIO (Conceive, Design, Implement, Operate) methodology. Each instructional tier tackles a genuine unresolved challenge from the original research: extracting graph-based meaning from visual molecular representations, dynamically acquiring graph architectures rather than utilizing static ones, extracting features without relying on labeled properties, and generalizing models to novel molecular classes while maintaining computational efficiency. The curriculum comprises 32 distinct lab exercises spanning 64 contact hours, structured into six sequential modules. It features criterion-based evaluations that explicitly accept well-documented unsuccessful trials, reflecting the original study's ablation experiments where techniques like pre-training, dynamic attention routing, and strategic sparsification yield distinct, quantifiable impacts. By utilizing open-source molecular datasets and a scaled-down version of the research architecture, the proposed system remains fully executable on standard educational laboratory equipment. Furthermore, the robust, full-scale reference metrics are utilized as benchmarks for analytical interpretation rather than mandatory performance targets.
